evidence: Wayback: 'Accueil - APN - Algerie' (2005-02); 'apn-dz.org - This website is for sale!' (2015-06); now a private detective agency in Ichikawa, Japan ('探偵事務所アーガス'). The Assemblee Populaire Nationale held this domain, let it lapse, and a third party registered it. It publishes a valid DMARC record, so leaving it in scores the detective agency's posture as Algeria's parliament.

Wayback: 'Asamblea Nacional' (2020-02); now 'ALEXISTOGEL: Bandar Togel Online', an Indonesian gambling site. Also carries a Wikidata P582 end time of 2023-01-04: this is the 2015-elected assembly whose mandate ended, and the domain went with it.

Never an institutional domain. Wayback shows 'Editorials in Hindi' (2022-06), an SEO blog; now a Bangladeshi casino. Wikidata P856 for President of India points at an ARTICLE on it (/powers-of-president-of-india-100-best-explain/), not a homepage. India's actual head-of-state domain, presidentofindia.gov.in, is separately present and correct.

Pakistan Press Foundation is an independent media NGO, not the Supreme Court of Pakistan, and Wayback shows it as PPF back to 2004. The court's own domain, supremecourt.gov.pk, is separately present in the frame.

The Supreme Tribunal of Justice 'in exile' - a rival body appointed by the opposition-held assembly, not the court exercising jurisdiction in Venezuela. The state institution, tsj.gob.ve, is separately present. Kept out to avoid counting Venezuela's judiciary twice; the exile tribunal is a real organisation but not the institution this frame is enumerating.

Carries a P576 date of 2026-07-01, but this is a routine dissolution before an election, not an abolition: Wikidata still describes it in the present tense as 'legislature of Kazakhstan', records no successor body, and parlam.kz currently serves the live parliament site. A blanket rule on P576 would have wrongly dropped a functioning parliament.
